caption:
NATIONAL GIRLS AND WOMEN IN SPORTS DAY!🩷

Being a woman in sports means learning how to take up space in rooms you once dreamed of entering. It means showing up as an athlete, a leader, a learner, and a creator, and sometimes all at once. From competing for Mizzou Softball and working in the sports world, I’ve seen firsthand how much strength, resilience, and purpose women bring to this industry.

Sports have given me confidence, discipline, and a platform to grow beyond the field. They’ve surrounded me with women who lead boldly, support loudly, and push boundaries without apology. Today is a reminder of how impactful it is when women invest in women, when girls see themselves represented, and when we continue to open doors wider for the next generation.

This space is powerful. This journey is meaningful. And SHE's On Deck.

caption:
In the blink of an eye, my college career has come to an end. It’s been hard to put into words what these past 4 years have meant to me. There’s so much I could say and not enough room to share it. The things we’ve accomplished throughout this journey is something I have always dreamed of and never imagined could be possible. Above all awards and accomplishments throughout my career, there’s nothing I will cherish more than the memories and friendships I’ve built. Ive been blessed with teammates these past 4 years who not only have a passion for the sport, but a genuine love and care for the people around them. Thank you for making everyday in the gym worth every second and pushing me to be the best I can be.

I want to especially thank @dawn3sullivan for taking a chance on me. 5 years ago I would never have imagined I’d be where I am today and with the opportunities I’ve been given and I can owe it to this woman. Since day one, you have believed in me and have carved a path for me to be the best version of myself. Thank you for giving me the opportunity to live out my dream of playing at the highest level at two amazing universities. I am forever grateful to have been coached by you and to have built a relationship that will last a lifetime.

 I also want to shoutout @jhennagabriel , @missrel7 , @thecamargofamily_ , and Cullen irons for being the absolute best assistant coaches. I have been able to grow tremendously as a player by all of your guidance. Each one of you holds so much love for your players not only as athletes but as people. You guys have poured so much into this program and these people and it’s been such an amazing experience learning, laughing, competing, and creating memories I will hold onto forever. 

I’m not nearly ready to say goodbye to this place and this program, but I know I can leave feeling proud of everything we have accomplished and the legacy left for futures to come! I hope you all out in the community of Columbia continue to show up and show out for this program and to keep Hearnes such a special place to be. 

My volleyball journey is not over yet! Onto this next chapter with many exciting things to come! MIZ 4life 💛🐯🖤

caption:
To say I’m proud to be a part of this group would be an understatement. We set a goal as a team at the start of the year, a goal that everyone bought into - us as athletes, our coaches, athletic trainers, dieticians, massage therapists - everyone. We all knew what it would take to stand on the line with the Nation’s best on November 22nd, so to see our hard work, belief and vision come to fruition is surreal. 

It’s no secret that if you want to be up there with the NCAA’s elite, simply doing ‘extras’ is not enough because everyone is doing that so sometimes a whole lot of heart and trust goes a long way. I am honoured to pull on this jersey, to show up in the dark every morning to practice and to spend my days with this team. 

Thank you @kylevermore for leading us from the front, for believing in us, for giving us all we need to be successful and for getting the Tiger women back on the National start line for the first time in almost a decade. 

Ok essay over. Let’s run this back one more time for the year, & on the biggest stage. Natties this Saturday 🐯

caption:
sound on! 🔊 i’m walking you through this entire process today 😘

THE GOAL: take my client back to her natural brunette, but keep some subtle dimension. the best part? we didn’t use a single drop of lightener!

her hair needed a serious break, so we worked with the highlights she already had. here’s how:
 1. prepped her hair with the k18 mist for strength and protection.
 2. isolated some of her existing highlights by applying @aluram hydrate and repair conditioning treatment and sealing them in foils.
 3. applied her new, rich brunette base color + separate mids/ends formula in between all the foils.

when someone is ready to really switch back to their natural, this is one of my favorite ways to do exactly that. some common terms for this process are: tint back, all over color and highlights (no bleach), reverse balayage, dimensional brunette, and many more!

📌 FORMULA BREAKDOWN for @megix10 stylists:
THE HIGHS: preserved pre-existing lightened hair, isolated in foils with @aluram hydrate and repair conditioning treatment
THE BASE: @megix10 6.0 + 5.71 + 12vol
THE LOWLIGHTS & MIDS/ENDS: @megix10 6.71 + 12 vol, used the same formula 🤍
ALL OVER GLOSS: applied after rinsing to seal and tone the blonde hair left in her hair, @megix10 103 + double fix + morph drops

caption:
It is with a heavy heart that I share the passing of my 17’s Head Coach and absolute legend, Ping Cao.

Playing for him remains one of my highest honors, and certainly an opportunity that was not available to just anyone. He had a keen eye for talent and potential, and always put his best foot forward to develop his athletes into the players and people we are today. Every 5+ hour practice, every critique, every coach-on-one, and every fingertip push-up (iykyk) will never be something I take for granted. I owe so much of where I am today to him. 

Rest in peace to a true icon in the volleyball community, and thank you for all the endless lessons that I’ve been able to carry with me throughout my career. No words will ever be able to describe how much you’ve impacted my life, and the lives of those who knew you. #Pingdomforever

🤍- “Jeh” :’)

caption: wow. having the opportunity to have Ping as a coach at 17 and a setting trainer since i was 13 was such a blessing. Ping always pushed me hard since day one, and he never let me stay complacent. he was super knowledgeable of the game, passionate, funny, and all around amazing. It was a dream come true to get to be one of his players and experience Pingdom. One thing Ping always told our team was “you have to want it more than anybody else wants it, you have to be willing to work”; I remind myself of that everyday. Everything I learned from Ping has carried into my life and volleyball journey. Ping emphasized hard work, discipline, grit, passion, determination, and drive. I will forever be grateful for Ping. Kaia Tanskanen voimisteli vakuuttavasti neliottelun finaaliin Jakartassa käynnissä olevissa telinevoimistelun MM-kisoissa. Suomalaisten kilpailuvuoro oli maanantaina, ja lopullisia tuloksia saatiin jännittää pitkälle tiistai-iltapäivään, kun naisten karsinnat 
kilpailtiin loppuun.

Lopulta Tanskanen oli neliottelun karsinnassa 16:s, kun 24 parasta jatkaa finaaliin. 💥

Tanskanen oli myös permannolla erittäin lähellä kahdeksan parhaan finaalia. Tällä telineellä sijoitus oli lopulta 11:s – kolmas varasija finaaliin ja vain 0,1 pistettä 8. sijasta (permannolla yht. 115 voimistelijaa). 😮‍💨🤏

caption:
Week 2! This week I found a tried Lebanese coffee for the first time. It was very VERY strong. Lowkey not terrible though. I visited the beach for the first time. It was a really pleasant walk but it’s a bit too chilly for laying out. It’s a lot of mid 60s highs with winds. Went for a hike near my house and it was surprisingly pretty for being 3 mins from my door. And then I got sick. In fact I’m still sick. Not as sick as I was but I’m not not sick rn. Once I recovered i started our CD collection for our car since there’s no Bluetooth. (Note in the video that the back window of said car will no longer go up anymore) I bought a Kacey Musgraves album and an Aretha album and they both bang. Finally, yesterday we played our first game and I went 2 innings, 4ks, 1 hit, 0 BBs out of the bullpen. My body hurts so bad.

While I was sick I watched the biographical comedy “Mo” by Mo Amer, a Palestinian comedian. I’m always hesitant to talk too much politics on IG because it can only be so productive, but between this show and the videos from the recent ceasefire, I am feeling really heartbroken for Palestine and especially what has happened these last 2 years. We will and should look back on this genocide as Americans, as humans, with so much shame and grief.

Anywhomst, I need to remember to try to get more videos of me throwing because most of my friends have never seen me play baseball. Now that I’m not sick or jet lagged, I’ll try to explore more this week

caption:
I never thought my senior season and college career would end this way. 30 minutes into our second SEC game, I tore my ACL, MCL, and meniscus. I’ve spent time feeling sorry for myself, struggling to understand how this could happen when everything finally felt like it was coming together. When I was playing my best soccer and when I had more love and passion for the sport than ever before. The truth is, it’s not fair. 

It’s not fair, but I can be proud of what I’ve proven on the field and the impact I’ve had on this program. I played every game like it was my last, so there’s nothing to regret. I know that my younger self would be proud, especially the 18-year-old version of me who came in as a walk-on, unsure if she was good enough to play at this level. She would be proud. 

So here’s to the next chapter. I know it will be defined by resilience and growth, and even though I still feel like I had more to give, I will have to channel that energy into something new. I’m so lucky to be surrounded by friends and family who are cheering me on as I take on this new challenge.

Shoutout to Kevin Coleman Jr. '22 and Jamal Roberts '23 on Mizzou’s HUGE win over Kansas! 🏈

Jamal Roberts: 13 carries for a career-high 143 yards, including a 63-yard touchdown run that iced the game.

Kevin Coleman Jr.: 10 catches for 126 yards and a touchdown, plus a clutch 3-yard, fourth-down score to close a 15-play, 75-yard drive.

caption:
over six years ago, i joined the aces fastpitch club. yesterday was the last time i stepped on the field wearing that jersey with my teammates. we’ve been chasing our dreams together for so long—celebrating the highs, learning from the lows, and holding each other through it all. it was never just about one of us. it was about all of us showing up, bringing energy, and competing with heart. yesterday, we did exactly that. the aces are the 2025 afcs national champions.

there were a lot of tears. and even though we’re heading off to different schools next month, i couldn’t imagine a more beautiful way to end this chapter. a true storybook finish.

to my girls—thank you for all the laughs, the long nights, the memories that i’ll carry with me forever. thank you for pushing me, believing in me, and making this ride something i’ll never forget. i genuinely love each of you with my whole heart. go be you, and know that wherever we all go, i’ll always be cheering you on.

thank you to every coach who’s poured into me, on and off the field. you’ve shaped the player and person i am.

to my family and friends—thank you for every cheer, every late night, every word of encouragement. mom, you’ve thought through every little thing and always been the calm in the storm. dad, thank you for being my biggest fan and for keeping me grounded. i wouldn’t be here without you. these memories will stay with me forever. next time you come to a game, you won’t be loading the truck or setting up the camera. you’ll just get to watch.

it’s time to rest and refuel. columbia, i’m coming. 🐯

caption:
Dear Select Softball,
I don’t even know how to begin this, because how do you say goodbye to something that’s been part of your soul for so long? This weekend, I stepped off the field for the last time as a select ball player. Closing this chapter hurts in a way I didn’t expect. It’s not just the end of a season. It’s the end of a version of me that grew up through every pitch, every dugout talk, and every triumph. You’ve been there through it all. You were the reason I fell in love with early mornings and late nights. You were why I learned the meaning of sacrifice. Giving up weekends, vacations, and sleep just to chase a dream. You taught me what it means to show up when I didn’t feel like it, to fight through slumps, to pick myself up after strikeouts, and to be just as proud of the small wins as the big ones.
Some of my most treasured moments in life happened in a dusty uniform, surrounded by teammates I now call sisters and coaches who believed in me even when I didn’t believe in myself. Select ball was never just about competition it was about growth, about heart, about grit. And now, as I turn the page and prepare for the next level, I carry all of that with me. The lessons, the bruises, the moments that made me they’re not going anywhere. They’re stitched into me like the seams of the ball I’ve held a thousand times. Thank you, softball, for being my constant, for giving me a place to belong, for teaching me how to lead, how to lose with grace, how to win with humility, and how to love something with my whole heart. Select ball may be over, but my love for you isn’t. Not even close. I’m walking into college with gratitude in my heart, fire in my soul, and a quiet promise to make every inning count because of everything you gave me.🤟🏻🤍🐯#DES

This past weekend, we welcomed over 100 youth football players for a day full of fun, mentorship, and high-level coaching — all powered by Jeremiah’s incredible staff, made up of collegiate athletes and elite coaches from across the state.

Every camper walked away with a custom T-shirt, backpack, lunch from Yoshi Hibachi Grill (@enjoyyoshi) and Urban Grill (@urbangrilleats) — and big smiles on their faces.

Thank you to our event sponsors @heirloomhospitality and @eplawwins for your incredible support. And a special thank you to Brett and @doapparelusa for consistently providing us with high-quality custom shirts that elevate every event we’re part of.

To everyone who showed up, gave back, and poured into the next generation — thank you. We’re already looking forward to next year!

caption:
This moment still feels like a dream. After 3 unforgettable years as a zebra, countless practices, early mornings, tough losses, big wins, and memories that will stay with me forever, we did it we are state champions. To go out on top my senior year is more than I ever could’ve hoped for. This team has been my family, this sport my passion, and this community my forever home. Every bruise, every grind, every late night bus ride was worth it for this feeling right here.

As I walk away from high school, I leave behind a part of myself the girl who fell in love with this game, who learned how to lead, to fight, to grow, and to believe. It’s not just about the trophy, it’s about the journey that got us here. I’m beyond proud of this team and forever grateful for the coaches, teammates, family, and friends who stood by me through it all.

Here’s to the end of one incredible chapter and the beginning of something new. But no matter where I go, I’ll always be a part of this team, and this win will live with me forever.🦓 #zebranation #senioryear #statechamps

• Conclusion of year 2✅

 - First year competing for Mizzou was filled with ups and downs, one far outweighing the other. I was unable to put together and find what was there in the fall semester when it mattered most. I finished the year with a mark of 17.81/58’5, far under what I had been hoping for/expecting. Although I had not obtained the athletic feats I had been hoping for, I have learned many life lessons through these trials. I will take this season on the chin, and will not squander the next three. 

• On a more positive note, I have made many new friends, and deepened relationships with some I had already had. I spent another year with my amazing girlfriend, and am one step closer to my degree ⚙️🛠️ 

Thank you Mom and Dad
Cheers to the next three years

caption:
March is national endometriosis awareness month and because God put it on my heart, I’ve decided to share my story. Roughly 2 1/2 years ago I was diagnosed with endometriosis. My journey with this disease began at the age of 12 when I sobbed through the hours of stabbing pain from my first period. From there, I was in monthly debilitating pain, sometimes missing school and practices. I pleaded with doctors for years most of whom told me it was normal or birth control would fix the problem. It took 7 years for me to finally receive a diagnosis. A few months later, I had surgery to hopefully relieve some of my pain. 

Unfortunately, surgery was unsuccessful and my disease has progressed. There have been days when I have sat in my car crying and begging God to take my pain away. I have said no to dozens of plans because my pain made moving nearly impossible. I have passed out from pain and blood loss. I have winced and collapsed in pain through more workouts than I can count.

That said, my story is not rare. 
There are thousands of women and young girls who know my pain and have been told that it’s “normal”. So I am not sharing my story for sympathy, instead I’m sharing it for them and in hopes that they would feel a little less alone. Because at 12 years old I remember how much I needed to know I wasn’t the only one who was suffering. 

To the women who relate, this pain is not normal. It’s ok to keep pushing to find the why. And remember, it will get better. Like I have, you will learn to manage it better and there will be people along the way to help on the days when you can’t do it alone. Despite what you may have been told, birth control is not your only option and there is help. Beyond that, there is healing that I’ve yet to find but believe exists. 

Above all else, God is good and I will praise him regardless. I believe there is purpose in my pain and that God has so much more in store for me. This disease is not my story, rather something God is using to bring myself and others closer to him. Whether I find healing or not, God wins. 

To anyone else who is struggling, reach out to me and know that God sees you, loves you and chose you. 
#endometriosis

On February 2nd, shortly after losing my match against Oklahoma State, I found out my papa had passed away the day before after battling for weeks in the hospital with pneumonia. 

February 2nd was the day I made a promise to myself that I would push through every ounce of adversity I would face for the rest of my life because I know he didn’t raise me to quit on myself and let all my hard work go to waste.

Now I know he was never able to watch me wrestle in a collegiate duel or compete in a tournament in person, but ever since he left, I’ve talked to him every day. Before every match, I ask God and him for guidance, for the ability to feel free, and to surrender the outcome , being okay with whatever the results may be.

Even though I didn’t finish at the top of the podium this year, I still proved to myself that I belong with all the top guys. Now that I’ve discovered myself and started to fall in love with the sport of wrestling again, I want to push myself as far as I can to put myself in the best possible position to win.

I’m thankful for all the adversity this season, and I love my team. Ready for next year.

caption:
Round 3 ✅

No sé cómo empezar a describir esta temporada, pero definitivamente la foto describe mi sentir. 
Esta temporada fue como volver a empezar, todo era nuevo otra vez. Me sentí tan llena, feliz, motivada, estuve llena de éxitos y con ansias de más. Desafortunada y tristemente no tuve el final de temporada que esperaba, yo y mis entrenadores esperábamos más, tristemente no se cumplió el objetivo que teníamos al principio de la temporada. 

Esta vez me toco aprender a la mala, y vaya que dolió y sigue doliendo, pero como diría mi mamá, de los errores se aprende dos veces y vaya que lo hice.  Ahora, sólo me queda reconocer y agradecer el gran progreso que he hecho, tanto en mis habilidades físicas como en las mentales, conectando cuerpo y mente. 
Casi siempre que competía tenía tanto miedo de cagarla, que la terminaba regando. Ahora puedo decir que ya compito sin miedo, más mía, más segura y para mí eso ya es ganar. 

Ahora toca poner la cabeza en alto y a seguir trabajando que aún quedan cosas por lograr. 
Last, but not least. I want to thank everyone who believed in me and still by my side. Thank you so much to my divers and coaches. ✨

At SoftWave by Molotherapy, we’re here to keep athletes moving pain-free so they can stay focused on what they love. Whether you’re throwing discus or just trying to get through the day without pain, we’ve got your back (and hips!).

caption:
Man what an experience. This camp is truly life changing and I’m so grateful for it. Before coming to this camp I have felt so distance from the Lord, so alone and in need of him. For the first time in a long time I have truly felt his presence. 

I learned that I am never alone and that God desires to be my everything. I am more than good enough for him, I am accepted by him, he does not care about my performance just my faithfulness. This camp also taught me how I can still worship him through my struggles and suffering. When we’re struggling and want the pain to go away we are desperate for anything. This honestly helped expose my true idols and that I didn’t have God at the center of my life. What the devil intended to use to harm me, God intended it for his good and his glory. 

UTC I am so thankful for this opportunity. I don’t think I have ever as cried as much as I did at this camp. To see the power of God working in this community was amazing. You have brought life long friends into my life as well as amazing memories. 

Lastly, to my team I am truly thankful for each and everyone of you, we couldn’t have made it through “The Special” without each other and I’m am proud of each and everyone of you guys. Through the grueling 20 hour long “Special”, you pushed me, encouraged me, were there for me and you helped show me that I can draw my strength from the Lord. I am so glad to have experienced this once in a lifetime opportunity with you all. Love you guys, Limitless gang 🔛🔝 

For with God nothing is ever impossible-Luke 1:37
